Compliance-as-code ends audit theater is not a slogan; it is a delivery position. We keep seeing the same economics: teams that internalize this spend their budget on value, while teams that ignore it spend on rework and explanations.

items: One framework-agnostic control register maps to SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS 4.0 and DORA simultaneously.
Failing-control workflows matter more than dashboards — findings need owners and dates.
DORA's third-party oversight is a data problem; treat the register as a governed product.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Where exactly does the evidence for each claim live — and can your auditor reach it without a project?
Who signs the go/no-go gate, and what evidence do they require before signing?
Show us a negative result you documented — the discipline is the product.

blocks.x: The expensive mistake is measurement retrofits: without the baseline locked in week one, every outcome claim becomes an argument instead of an audit, and the program loses its budget defense.

items: falsifiable criteria and locked baselines before build; the demo is the least important artifact.
named owners, run models and escalation paths agreed with the operating team, not for it.
replay trails, control tests and documentation as artifacts of the build — never reconstructed.

blocks.x: Audit preparation effort typically falls 60-80% under evidence automation.
